title: Luke Evans Makes Broadway Debut As 'Sweet Transvestite' In 'The Rocky Horror Show' - NewsBreak
text:
By Ryan Kwon ,
10 hours ago Luke Evans is leading a star-studded cast into the world of fishnets and extraterrestrial madness as the Roundabout Theatre Company production of The Rocky Horror Show .
The highly anticipated revival of Richard O’Brien ’s cult-classic musical arrives at the historic Studio 54 for a strictly limited 12-week run.
Directed by Tony Award winner Sam Pinkleton , known for his work on Oh, Mary! , the production is scheduled to officially open on April 23. The engagement is currently slated to run through June 21, offering audiences a rare opportunity to see Evans make his Broadway debut in the iconic role of Dr. Frank-N-Furter.
The ensemble features a significant number of performers, many of whom are marking their first appearances on a Broadway stage. Joining Evans in their debuts are Juliette Lewis as Magenta, Harvey Guillén as Eddie and Dr. Scott, Josh Rivera as Rocky and Golden Globe winner Michaela Jaé Rodriguez as Columbia.
The “eccentric crew” is rounded out by veteran performers, including Rachel Dratch as the Narrator, Andrew Durand as Brad, Stephanie Hsu as Janet and Amber Gray as Riff Raff. The company also features Renée Albulario , Anania , Boy Radio , Caleb Quezon , Andres Quintero , Larkin Reilly , Paul Soileau and John Yi .
The creative vision for this revival is supported by choreographer Ani Taj and music director Kris Kukul , who also provided the orchestrations. Brian Ronan serves as the sound designer, with hair and makeup design by Alberto “Albee” Alvarado .

Rocky Horror follows the misadventures of “sweethearts” Brad and Janet, whose night takes a “bizarre turn” after their car breaks down during a storm. Their search for a telephone leads them to the doorstep of Frank-N-Furter, where they are introduced to a household of characters and the creation of a perfect man, Rocky.
The production features the legendary book, music and lyrics by O’Brien, including the “iconic songs” that have defined the musical’s 50-year legacy. Audiences can expect to hear classics such as “Dammit Janet,” “Touch-A, Touch-A, Touch Me,” “Sweet Transvestite” and the participatory favorite “Time Warp.”
